summary.intent: Work through the NEXT-WORK plan for the Callisto release tool (cleanup, test debt, SYS-RETRY, SYS-NAPI, derive.rs split), then pivot to making status/version/release fast on large monorepos and absorb the michi 0.6 handoff.
summary.outcome: Opened and merged a series of PRs: SYS-RETRY fix, mixed-routing test, docs refresh, init/template moves, SYS-NAPI, derive.rs split, and a performance stack (#327, #328, #330, #333) that replaced history scans with tree-id comparison. ADR 13 (tag annotation hints) is open as a proposal. Michi 0.6 adoption is analyzed but not started.

repo: Plan/tracking files such as NEXT-WORK.md must stay local (.claude/plans/, excluded via .git/info/exclude) and never go in a commit or PR; PR #201 was closed for this reason.
`just ci` is the gate; its wrapper script can exit 0 even when the log shows failure, so read the log's own `exit=` line (a real failure showed exit=100). Coverage gate is 90%.

Rerun selection previously treated a tag on HEAD as 'released', which was the SYS-RETRY defect. Packages tagged at HEAD now have every operation observed (registry, tag, GitHub release); a tag on an older commit settles the version without contacting providers.
The release harness fakes gh, cargo and registry reads, which hid bugs earlier. Real-tool tests (real jq, real binary) are needed for template work like SYS-NAPI.
Generated workflow templates run on macOS bash without `mapfile`, so use portable while-read loops.
The intent omits `artifactSlots` when empty, so jq `.artifactSlots[]` iterates null; the dry-run report flattens the intent with envelope fields that must be stripped to get the plain intent.
Stacked PRs are linked with `gh stack`; a closed PR in a stack blocks relinking, so unstack and recreate.
Commits/PRs must not include a session link per AGENTS.md; ADRs must be marked Proposed until the implementing PR merges.
System git is the chosen backend (ADR 5). gix was benchmarked: gix-pack caches only the final delta-resolved object, so history walks are 3-10x slower than `git log` on wide trees; keep gix out.
Tag ownership manifest reads are a safety check against renamed or removed packages adopting a bare-named tag, not waste, so they should not be skipped on name uniqueness.
The 'changed since last tag' meaning is now net change (tree id comparison); a reverted edit no longer counts as changed, and this is stated in the spec.

code.finding: Callisto's Git access uses the system git binary here, so there is no gix cache to tune in production code.
IdentityIndex::native_names, native_name and platforms_of scan the whole name map per package (quadratic, about 12% of status at 10,000 packages); fixed with a mutex-backed reverse index cache.
The locator probes three canonical manifest files per directory and then re-opens each manifest; parallel reading and passing content on removed the double read.

Release derivation was split into stage functions with OpIndex holding the prerequisite maps (including uploads_by_package), protected by insta characterization snapshots and error-path tests added first.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first, then fix, and prove a new test can fail by mutating the source (done for the W1 and R3 tests).
For pure refactors, commit snapshot/characterization tests on the old code first, then do the mechanical move and confirm snapshots pass unchanged.

Profile with a corrected, uncontended machine before trusting numbers; noisy timings and warm second passes misled earlier conclusions, and the assistant retracted two claims after measuring properly.
Sandbox rejects inline env, heredocs and scripts mentioning git; write scripts to temp files, use Edit/Write tools, and only edit inside the current worktree.
Run an independent review agent on risky PRs such as #202 while other work proceeds.
Use throwaway spike crates outside the repo to compare libraries (gix, git2) before adopting a dependency.

friction: The plan file was initially committed in PR #201 contrary to the user's intent for local tracking, requiring a close and relocation.
Sandbox restrictions (inline env, heredocs, git-mentioning scripts, edits outside the current worktree) forced many workarounds, including switching worktrees to edit docs.
Background sessions could not edit the shared checkout, so the plan status was not updated in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md.
CI failures required follow-up edits: three existing tests assumed tag-on-HEAD means released, plus a stray blank line in the moved tests.
Profiling noise from another process compiling on the machine, and an incomplete first profile, produced misleading numbers.
A push to PR #330 was rejected as non-fast-forward and needed a rebase; closing #331 forced unstacking and relinking the stack.
gh PR bodies with escaped backticks in quoted heredocs rendered literal backslashes and had to be fixed.
open_items: Branch cleanup (docs/next-work-plan, docs/spec-rewrite, fix/native-resolution, about 35 local branches) awaits per-branch user approval.
W1 real-service credential check needs a decision on where it runs in CI; W11 verification needs credentials and an approved run.
D01-blocked work (SYS-MATURIN, W9) and the W10 decisions (distinct target declaration graph edges, Python dev group cascade) await the user.
Follow-up edits to T08-RETRY entries in the roadmap, plan JSON and guide once #202 merges; PR #204 still lists SYS-RETRY.
Independent review findings on #202 (multi-paragraph tag, dependent tagged at HEAD with untagged dependency) were being addressed; final status is not shown in the transcript.
Lanes C (SYS-PYFILES, SYS-PYROUTES, redacted provider output), D SYS-BARRIER and F (R1 walk.rs::build) not started.
ADR 13 (tag annotation hints) PR is open as Proposed and needs the user's acceptance before implementation.
Release PR #316 is stale (7 changesets vs 9 pending) and must be regenerated before merging 0.14.0.
The settle_issued window bugs (restarts wait per confirmation, counts only sleeps) remain on main; plan is to fix via michi 0.6 poll_step with deadline_group.
Michi 0.6 trial not started; npm 0.6.0 is held until 2026-10-24 02:55 UTC and ready_by_edge awaits michi-graph PR #48; the org NPM_TOKEN is the deprecated bypass-2FA type, keeping OIDC on the list.
Possible upstream gix-pack issue (cache intermediate delta bases) with a wide-tree benchmark, if the user wants it drafted.
